definitions.explanation: A person who composes waka ({和歌|わか}) or tanka ({短歌|たんか}), traditional Japanese poetry forms. Used both historically for classical poets and for modern tanka practitioners.

examples.japanese: {有名|ゆうめい}な{歌人|かじん}の{作品|さくひん}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: To read the works of a famous waka poet.

examples.japanese: {紀貫之|きのつらゆき}は{平安|へいあん}{時代|じだい}を{代表|だいひょう}する{歌人|かじん}だ。
examples.english: Ki no Tsurayuki is a representative waka poet of the Heian period.

examples.japanese: {現代|げんだい}の{歌人|かじん}たちは、{日常|にちじょう}の{言葉|ことば}を{使|つか}って{新|あたら}しい{短歌|たんか}を{生|う}み{出|だ}している。
examples.english: Modern tanka poets are creating new tanka using everyday language.

notes:
Specifically refers to a poet who writes {和歌|わか} (waka) or {短歌|たんか} (tanka), the traditional 31-syllable Japanese poem form. Composed of {歌|か} (song/poem) + {人|じん} (person).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歌人|かじん}の{歌集|かしゅう}: a poet's collection of tanka
- {近代|きんだい}{歌人|かじん}: modern-era waka poet
- {女流|じょりゅう}{歌人|かじん}: female waka poet
- {宮廷|きゅうてい}{歌人|かじん}: court poet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {俳人|はいじん}: haiku poet — a poet who writes haiku
- {詩人|しじん}: poet — a general term for any poet, especially those writing modern free verse
- {歌手|かしゅ}: singer — a different word entirely, not to be confused with {歌人|かじん}

NOTE:
Do not confuse {歌人|かじん} with the homophone {佳人|かじん} (a beautiful woman). The {歌人|かじん} tradition stretches from the {万葉集|まんようしゅう} era to the present day, with modern {歌人|かじん} continuing to innovate within the 5-7-5-7-7 syllable form.
